title: New Jersey good cause eviction grounds (N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.1)
requirement: A residential tenant may be removed only if the landlord proves one of the statutory good causes in Superior Court. Owner-occupied premises with not more than two rental units and certain family-occupied units are excluded.
coverage_conditions: All residential tenancies, except owner-occupied premises with not more than two rental units, transient or seasonal hotel or guest house rooms, and units held in trust for or occupied by an immediate family member of the owner who has a developmental disability.

applicability.per_tenancy: A dwelling unit held in trust for, or permanently occupied by, an immediate family member of the owner who has a developmental disability.
coverage_quotes: other than (1) owner-occupied premises with not more than two rental units or a hotel, motel or other guest house or part thereof rented to a transient guest or seasonal tenant; (2) a dwelling unit which is held in trust on behalf of a member of the immediate family of the person or persons establishing the trust, provided that the member of the immediate family on whose behalf the trust is established permanently occupies the unit; and (3) a dwelling unit which is permanently occupied by a member of the immediate family of the owner of that unit, provided, however, that exception (2) or (3) shall apply only in cases in which the member of the immediate family has a developmental disability

exemptions: Owner-occupied premises with not more than two rental units; hotels, motels or guest houses rented to transient or seasonal guests; units held in trust for or permanently occupied by a family member of the owner with a developmental disability.
quoted_span: except upon establishment of one of the following grounds as good cause: a. The person fails to pay rent due and owing under the lease whether the same be oral or written
